system.name: Hyrax
system.one_liner: a fail-in-place server operation system that lets degraded cloud servers keep running with reduced capacity instead of full repair

components.name: Server Health Monitor
components.role: detects server health issues such as NVMe read errors and follows the offlining workflow

components.name: Diagnostics
components.role: receives the health alert from SHM and reports the failing component for a policy decision

components.name: Hyrax Policy
components.role: new policy engine that decides the remediation/offlining action for a diagnosed component

components.name: Hyrax Inventory
components.role: tracks component and server offlining/degradation state, informs downstream scheduling and health monitoring

components.name: VM Scheduler
components.role: schedules VMs onto servers, informed by Hyrax Inventory about a server's reduced capacity

components.name: Hardware Inventory
components.role: existing inventory of hardware components feeding data into Hyrax Inventory

components.name: Online
components.role: region of the control plane comprising components that operate while the server stays online

components.name: Offline
components.role: region of the control plane comprising components that operate once the server/component is taken offline

flows.what: reports a detected health issue (e.g. NVMe read errors) for diagnosis
reports the failing component for a policy decision
updated capacity/inventory state used for VM placement
feedback closing the loop back to health monitoring

content.key_idea: A server health event flows through Diagnostics and the new Hyrax Policy engine to update Hyrax Inventory, which adjusts VM scheduling and reports back, closing the remediation loop.
content.reading_order: Numbered steps 1-6 trace a loop: Server Health Monitor to Diagnostics to Hyrax Policy to Hyrax Inventory to VM Scheduler and back to Server Health Monitor.

summary: This figure gives a simplified view of Hyrax's control plane within Microsoft Azure, walking through one SSD-failure example via six numbered steps. (1) The existing Server Health Monitor detects NVMe read errors and signals Diagnostics, which (2) reports the failing component to the newly added Hyrax Policy engine; Server Health Monitor and Diagnostics are modified existing systems (gold borders), while Hyrax Policy is a new control-plane system (red border). After an unlabeled step (3) shown as interaction with a gear icon, Hyrax Policy (4) updates the also-new Hyrax Inventory, which (5) informs the modified VM Scheduler of the server's reduced capacity and (6) reports back to the Server Health Monitor, closing the loop; a separate, untouched Hardware Inventory box also feeds Hyrax Inventory. A dashed line and shading separate Online from Offline components, and a legend explains the gold/red border colors.
summary_zh: 该图简化展示 Hyrax 控制平面：健康监控器检测故障并通知诊断模块，交由新建的 Hyrax Policy 决策，更新 Hyrax Inventory，再通知 VM 调度器并反馈给健康监控器，图例区分改造旧系统(金框)与全新系统(红框)。
notes: Step (3), an interaction between Hyrax Policy and an unlabeled green gear icon, is not named in the figure or in the available paragraph text, so it is omitted from components/flows.
